# dsh-perf-hud

A transparent, draggable performance HUD for the DeepSeek Harness web UI:
**CPU / GPU / memory usage

**, plus the **CPU package temperature** when the
optional helper is installed.
## Highlights

- **Fully transparent** — no card background, no border. Just three rows of text
floating over the i

nterface, with a soft halo so it stays readable on any
content.
- **Drag it anywhere.** On release i

t anchors to the nearest window corner, so
maximising, restoring or resizing the window keeps it exa

ctly where you put
it. Double-click resets to the top-right, arrow keys nudge it, and the chevron
th

at appears on hover collapses it to a single row.
- **Load-aware colours** — usage turns amber at 70

% and red at 90%; temperature
at 78 °C / 88 °C. Stale readings dim the whole card instead of flashin

g a fake
zero.
- **Theme-aware** — only `--dsw-alias-*` tokens, so it follows light, dark and
any cu

stom theme.
- **Local only** — the metrics route answers loopback, same-origin requests and
returns
403 for everything else. Nothing is uploaded.
## Requirements

- **Windows 10/11.** The GPU counters, the PowerShell worker and the temperature
helper are Windows-

specific.
- DeepSeek Harness with the web UI.

## What it reads
| Metric | Source |

| CPU usage | `node:os` CPU-time deltas, once a second |
| Memory usage | `os.totalmem()` / `os.free

mem()` — same definition as Task Manager's "In use" |
| GPU usage | Windows `GPU Engine` performance

counters, busiest engine (what Task Manager reports) |
| CPU temperature | optional helper — LibreH

ardwareMonitor's `CPU Package` sensor |
| GPU temperature | only when the GPU exposes a temperature
sensor; most integrated GPUs do not, so the cell shows `—` |
## Temperatures (optional)

The plugin works out of the box; without the helper both temperature cells show
`—`. For the real CP

U package temperature, run **once** (it asks for
administrator rights):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
That script downloads and sets up:

- **LibreHardwareMonitor 0.9.6** (portable, library only) — reads the sensors;
- **PawnIO 2.2.0**, a

signed kernel driver — required to read MSRs while Windows
"Memory integrity" (HVCI) stays enabled,

ON file about every 0.4 s;
- a scheduled task **`DSH Perf Sensor`** (at logon, highest privileges, n

o
window), so it never asks again.

Files go to `D:\DSHTools` when that drive exists, otherwise
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\DSHTools`. The plugin re
ads either location.

Measured overhead on an 8-core laptop: **0.08 % of one core and ~87 MB of RAM**
for the helper — it
is mostly waiting on the driver, not burning CPU.

## Limitations

- Windows only.
- GPU temperatures need a dedicated sensor; Intel integrated GPUs do not expose
one,

and the CPU package temperature is the closest reference (same die).
- The card floats **inside the

Harness window**, not as a separate
always-on-top desktop window.
